cells.tense: You're moving clean from what you actually feel, and the pattern work is where that lands.
cells.ask: Name one step whose only reason is that you want it. Take it before the day is over.
cells.core: You're on this because it stays true after the feeling drops. You strip a situation down to its moving parts, and where other people stall on the surface, the lines underneath are where you put your hands. That's not coldness. It's trusting the thing enough to find its spine.\n\nTake something you're carrying right now. Not the story you tell about it — the two or three parts that are actually pulling: what holds, what moves if nothing gets in the way. Say them out loud, plain, then pick one thing you'd do before the day ends without seeing how it comes out. Seeing the whole road was not the engine. The step is.
cells.sheetLine: You move best from what's real, and you don't need the whole road.
cells.verb: Moving at it until the thing is real, with or without the feeling.
cells.place: Working the pattern clean, where the lines that hold are the lines that move.

cells.tense: You'll have the whole thing worked out in your head before you take a step you could take right now.
cells.ask: Say what you know, what you don't, and what's still being decided. Three lines. Stop there for the day.
cells.core: You're keeping the pattern open longer than it needs to be open, using the shape of it as the room — when what you actually want is to be somewhere that works. You've got the mechanism, the two versions of how this turns out, and the step still not taken. The figuring stays interesting, and the ground stays untouched. More thinking won't produce the next move.\n\nTake one stand: what you know, what you're actually unsure of, and what's still being decided. Write the three lines or say them aloud, then leave them alone today. Notice the pull to add one more layer. That pull is the thing, not the plan. Your sense of timing is good. It just has to land somewhere.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern has to land somewhere, or it's all story.
cells.verb: Moving at it until the thing is real, with or without the feeling.
cells.place: Working the pattern clean, where the lines that hold are the lines that move.

cells.tense: You stopped moving before you knew what this was, and you can't tell whether that's still true.
cells.ask: Clear one thing that's over — a note you've been keeping, an item you've stopped using. One, today.
cells.core: You can see the shape and you're not making first contact. The pattern lives in the mind and the body hasn't moved, and the not-moving has started to look like method. What you can see is bigger than what you're spending.\n\nThat isn't a failing of wanting. Something here finished and it hasn't landed as finished. Take one thing that's over — a note, a thing you kept in case, something you no longer use — and close it plainly today. You don't have to know what takes its place, and you don't have to feel something first. Clear one thing, then let the next hour be whatever it is.
cells.sheetLine: Stop waiting for going to feel like something. Clear it, then go.
cells.verb: Moving at it until the thing is real, with or without the feeling.
cells.place: Working the pattern clean, where the lines that hold are the lines that move.

cells.tense: The moving is happening in how you arrange the week, and you've been calling it a phase.
cells.ask: Write down what you've done in the last two weeks. Look for the one direction it kept going.
cells.core: You've been steering and calling it waiting. The hours go a certain way — the same few things get kept, the rest get set down, and the shape of that is a direction whether or not it has a name. Answers about what comes next aren't the hold-up. The hold-up is claiming the one you're living.\n\nSomewhere under the careful thinking there's a line that's been running — a pull that doesn't need the right mood, just the next step along it. Pick one thing on that line and call it yours out loud, to yourself or to someone who'd hear it. That's the whole move. The rest is hurry.
cells.sheetLine: You've been moving this whole time. Call it yours.
cells.verb: Moving at it until the thing is real, with or without the feeling.
cells.place: Working the pattern clean, where the lines that hold are the lines that move.

attempts.check: The one claim the record doesn't back is anything positive about where the low points of too little drive came from, or what someone once felt about starting; I name the threshold and the stall and stop. A reader could fairly say the pattern-seeing is exactly what keeps them from moving rather than what they're moving on, so I keep Drive as the card and Abstraction as the place and let the cards stay where they are. The asks name one next step, one act seen from the outside, one clear ending, one condition stated — they'd survive if the reading is wrong about why. The sentence that serves me more than the person is 'you were always the one already building' — the house would swallow it and the record doesn't.
